### MYQORZO® (aficamten) Receives ASMR III Rating from the HAS (French National Authority for Health) for the Treatment of Symptomatic Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Adults


November 10, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s206.q4cdn.com/793207125/files/doc_news/MYQORZO-aficamten-Receives-ASMR-III-Rating-from-the-HAS-French-National-Authority-for-Health-for-the-Treatment-of-Symptomatic-Obstruc-0GIRK.pdf)


PARIS, November 10, 2026 – Cytokinetics, Incorporated (Nasdaq: CYTK) today announced that the Transparency Committee of the French National Authority for Health (Haute Autorité de Santé, HAS) has granted MYQORZO® ( *aficamten* ) a significant Medical Benefit (Service Médical Rendu, SMR) rating and an ASMR III rating (moderate improvement in medical benefit) for the full scope of its marketing authorization, namely the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) in New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classes II and III.1


“This decision marks an important milestone for Cytokinetics in France,” said Sandra Fournier, General Manager of Cytokinetics France. “It recognizes the important contribution of MYQORZO® to the management of obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in adults and will support expanding access for patients struggling with the daily burden of this disease.”


The Committee based its assessment on SEQUOIA-HCM2 and MAPLE-HCM3, the Phase 3 clinical trials of *aficamten* in oHCM. In SEQUOIA-HCM, MYQORZO® demonstrated superiority over placebo in improving exercise capacity, clinical symptoms, and quality of life, as well as reducing the duration of eligibility for septal reduction therapy. In MAPLE-HCM, MYQORZO® demonstrated superiority over *metoprolol* in improving exercise capacity, clinical symptoms and quality of life.


The Committee also noted the safety profile based on safety data from the clinical trials.


The HAS also recognized the benefits observed in improving functional capacity, symptoms and quality of life, as assessed using the NYHA functional classification and the disease-specific Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS).


Cytokinetics obtained its authorization to operate as a pharmaceutical establishment (établissement pharmaceutique exploitant) in France on August 31, 2026, and continues to pursue its commitment to providing long-term support to healthcare professionals and their patients in the region.


**MYQORZO® is a prescription-only medicine. This press release is intended for healthcare professionals and specialist media.**


**For full details of the Transparency Committee’s assessment, please refer to the complete HAS Transparency Committee opinion:**[https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/p_4592681/fr/myqorzo-aficamten](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/p_4592681/fr/myqorzo-aficamten)


**About** **MYQORZO® ( *aficamten* )**


MYQORZO® ( *aficamten* ) **** is a cardiac myosin inhibitor approved in the U.S., China and European Union, United Kingdom and Canada for the treatment of symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM).


**About Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy**


Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a disease in which the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick. HCM can be obstructive when thickened muscle blocks blood flow, or non-obstructive, when blood flow is not blocked but heart function is still affected. In obstructive HCM, the thickening of cardiac muscle leads to the inside of the left ventricle becoming smaller, stiffer and less able to relax and fill with blood. Ultimately, HCM limits the heart’s pumping function, leading to reduced exercise capacity and a variety of symptoms.


HCM is the most common monogenic inherited cardiovascular disorder, affecting approximately one out of 350 individuals worldwide.4


Approximately half of patients with HCM have obstructive HCM (oHCM) and half have non-obstructive HCM (nHCM).5


People with HCM are at high risk of also developing cardiovascular complications including atrial fibrillation, stroke and mitral valve disease.6 People with HCM are at risk for potentially fatal ventricular arrhythmias and it is one of the leading causes of sudden cardiac death in younger people or athletes.7 A subset of patients with HCM are at high risk of progressive disease leading to dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure necessitating cardiac transplantation.
